subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 17, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 17, 2026

The development team has been busy addressing critical updates and improvements across the AcreetionOS ecosystem. Recent activity shows community merges focused on fixing geocode-glib update conflicts, which will improve system stability for users relying on geolocation services. The packaget build changes ensure smoother package management and prevent the GLib geo-related errors that were affecting some installations.

Major kernel development is underway as the Linux 7.2 kernel has officially been released, with the team preparing to integrate these latest improvements into upcoming AcreetionOS builds. The release notes indicate significant performance and security enhancements that will benefit our users. Linux kernel 7.2 is expected to bring improved hardware support and better power management capabilities.

We have successfully resolved a critical GitLab mirror issue that affected multiple repositories including acreetionos, acreetionos-archiso, acreetionos-news-tracker, acreetionos-terminal, and acreetionos-appstore. Darren Clift confirmed that the deploy key fix has been implemented across all projects, ensuring that future updates will sync properly between GitHub and GitLab. This fix eliminates the breaking changes that were preventing proper mirroring.

The AcreetionOS AppStore received significant feature updates with the addition of a new settings system, AUR sidebar toggle, grid view options, and AppImage auto-registration capabilities. Natalie Spiva led the implementation of these user-requested features, making the app management experience more intuitive and flexible for the community. These enhancements demonstrate the team's commitment to improving user experience.

Firefox UBlock Origin has been properly integrated into the AcreetionOS-Xlibre build, addressing the previous omission that left users without essential privacy protection extensions by default. The intelligence sync process continues to update our newsletter archives and wiki guides, ensuring documentation stays current with development progress. Both Natalie and Darren have been actively committing improvements to various system components.

The Python packaging council has announced its candidates for the upcoming election, reflecting the broader open-source community's ongoing governance discussions that impact development decisions across Linux distributions. Security remains a priority with recent advisories covering updates from AlmaLinux, Debian, and other distributions including .NET versions, bind, dracut, and chromium packages that we monitor for integration opportunities.

Community engagement continues to thrive with active discussions on the Discord server and regular contributions to both GitHub and GitLab repositories. The dual leadership approach of Natalie focusing on frontend features while Darren handles the infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines demonstrates effective distributed development practices that keep AcreetionOS stable and innovative.

Looking ahead, the team is preparing to build the next ISO release incorporating the resolved mirror configurations and latest feature additions from the AppStore updates. Users can expect improved installation reliability and enhanced user interface options in the upcoming version. The development roadmap continues to prioritize user freedom, privacy, and system stability as core AcreetionOS values.

Thank you for your continued support of this community-driven project. For questions or assistance, please visit our Discord community at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 or check the updated documentation on acreetionos.org.
